JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 17-09-2023, in the early morning between 2.00 a.m. to 2.10 a.m., when the petitioner was traveling on the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KK-6021 as a pillion rider, along with his friends by name Rishav V. Tanuk and Aditya Parmar, the same being ridden by Aditya Parmar, near Sanjaynagar 80 feet road.

When they reached near 4th cross, Sanjaynagar, at that time the driver of Suzuki Wagon R VXI car bearing Reg. No.TN-66-AE-1800 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and suddenly turned to the right side without any indication.

The rider of petitioner's motorcycle, which was behind the car, could not avoid his motorcycle colliding with the said car on its right side and dashed to another car bearing No.KA-03-AD-0461,
which was parked on the side of the road.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to M.S. Ramaiah Memorial Hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident he was student.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby he has not been able to concentrate on his studies.
The R.T. Nagar Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Section 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.

It has denied for having insured the Suzuki Wagon R VXI car bearing Reg.
No.TN-66-AE-1800 and it is subject to confirmation from the concerned branch of this respondent Suyash Rathod vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190535101/
2 and the liability of this respondent if any is subject to terms, conditions and limitations of policy of insurance, issued in favour of the respondent No.2 and in accordance with the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act.

sentences.text: Further it is contended that, the car bearing No.TN-66-AE-1800 was being driven by its driver without possessing valid and effective driving licence, permit and fitness certificate, as on the date of the alleged accident.
As there is breach of terms and conditions of the policy, this respondent is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.2.

Further it is contended that,
the petitioner was pillion rider of the motorcycle, totally 3 persons were traveling on the bike.
Due to over load they fell down on the road at 2.00 a.m. in midnight.
The time goes to show that, the rider and pillion riders were under influence of the alcohol.
Hence, rider has lost control over the bike and hit to the car bearing No.TN-66-AE-1800 and thereafter hit to the another car bearing No.KA-03-AD-0461.
More over all are under teenage, they were not wearing helmet and did not hold driving licence and insurance policy with respect to said motorcycle.
Hence, the alleged has taken place due to negligence on the part of the rider of motorcycle and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of car bearing No.TN-66-AE-1800.
Further it is contended that, the driver of the Omni car had also contributed to the cause of alleged accident and was guilty of contributory negligence.
All three vehicles have got damaged on the front portion and the accident has taken place in the junction.
Hence, all the three vehicles have caused the accident.
But, the petitioner has not made the owner and insurer of said vehicles as party to the present proceedings.
The owner and insurer of car bearing No.KA-03-AD-0461 (LMV) and owner and insurer of motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KK-6021 are necessary party to the present proceedings.

Further it has denied the age,
income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by the petitioner.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. Whereas, the respondent No.2 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
He has contended that, he is the registered owner of the car bearing No.TN-66-AE-1800 and the said car was insured with respondent No.1 and the said policy was valid from 25-06- 2023 to 24-06-2024.
Further it is contended that, his son who was driving the said car was holding valid driving licence and the vehicle was covered with valid insurance policy, at the time of alleged accident.
Further it is contended that, he has not violated any terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
At the time of accident the driver of offending vehicle was driving the same with great care and caution.

There was a contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner, as three persons were riding on the said two-wheeler, which was permissible for only two persons and they were not wearing helmet which is contravention of law.
Further it is contended that, at the time of accident the offending vehicle was insured by the respondent No.1 insurance company.
As such, the respondent No.2 is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
For the above denials and contentions, he has prayed to dismiss the petition.

sentences.text: In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 18 documents as Ex.P.1 to 18.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is certified copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is certified copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is certified copy of police notice, Ex.P.4 is certified copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.5 is certified copy of sketch, Ex.P.6 is certified copy of notice under Section 133 of Motor Vehicles Act, Ex.P.7 is certified copy of reply to notice under Section 133 of Motor Vehicles Act, Ex.P.8 is certified copy of indemnity bond, Ex.P.9 is certified copy of Motor Vehicles Accident report, Ex.P.10 is certified copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.11 is notarized copy of Aadhar card,
Ex.P.12 is notarized copy of PAN card, Ex.P.13 is discharge summary, Ex.P.14 is discharge summary issued by Suyog Hospital, Ex.P.15 is outpatient case sheet, Ex.P.16 are medical bills (total 12),
Ex.P.17 is OPD slip with clinical note and Ex.P.18 is x-ray.

12. On meticulously going through the above police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 12, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.TN-66-AE-1800 and suddenly turning the same to the right side without giving any indication.

Due to which, the rider of petitioner's motorcycle, who was riding his motorcycle behind the said car, could not avoid colliding with the said car on its right side and then dashed to another car bearing No.KA-03-AD-0461, which was parked on the side of the road.
Due to said impact the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

The investigation officer in his final report/charge-sheet, which is produced and got marked as Ex.P.18 in connected matter M.V.C.No.8291/2023, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg.
No.TN-66-AE-1800 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

13. At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.1 in respect of car bearing Reg.
No.TN-66-AE-1800 and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

But, the respondent No.1 & 2 have specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KK-6021 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of car bearing Reg. No.TN-66-AE-1800.

Further it is contended that, the petitioner in collusion with the police authorities and owner of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KK-6021 has got registered a false case against the driver of car bearing Reg.
No.TN-66-AE-1800, to get wrongful gain from the respondents.
But, the respondents have failed to establish the said contentions.

Except the self serving statements of R.W.1, who is representative/Deputy Manager of respondent No.1 insurance company, there is no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondents to establish the above contentions.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.TN-66-AE-1800 and suddenly turning the same to the right side without any indication.

Due to which, the rider of motorcycle, which was Suyash Rathod vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190535101/
5 behind the said car, could not avoid colliding with the said car to its right side and then dashing the same to another car bearing No.KA- 03-AD-0461, which was parked on the side of the road.

sentences.text: Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross- examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-KK-6021 or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.
14. But, it is pertinent to note that, admittedly, at the time of accident the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04- KK-6021 was riding the same along with two pillion riders.

There are every chances that, due to three persons traveling on a motorcycle, which is meant for two persons, there would be congestion to the rider of said motorcycle and he might have lost control resulting in the accident.

The petitioner being fully aware that, the said vehicle is meant for traveling of two persons,
he has taken risk of traveling triple on the said motorcycle.

Hence, this Court is of the opinion that,
the petitioner is also liable for contributory negligence in the cause of accident.

But, as there is no evidence on record to show that, the very act of three persons riding on the motorcycle has directly contributed either to the accident or to the impact of the accident upon the victim, this Court is of the opinion that, holding the petitioner liable for contributory negligence to the extent of 10% would be justified and it will meet the ends of justice.

15. The Ex.P.4 spot mahazar and Ex.P.5 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the right side of the road, near 4th cross, 80 feet road, Sanjaynagara, Bengaluru, in between the offending car bearing Reg. No.TN-66-AE-1800 and motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KK- 6021 of the petitioner.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.9, the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident is not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KK-6021, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.

Further, the investigation officer in his final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.TN-66-AE- 1800 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge- sheet has not been challenged either by the driver or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.TN-66-AE-1800.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records,
regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident,
negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

16. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.10 wound certificate and Ex.P.13 and 14 discharge summaries, Ex.P.15 out-patient case sheet, Ex.P.17 OPD slip with clinical note and Ex.P.18 x-ray, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in the road traffic accident.

The petitioner has sustained 1) displaced intraarticular radius fracture left forearm, 2) displaced ulnar styloid fracture, 3) dislocated 2, 3, 4th carpametacarpal joints with dorsal metacarpal Suyash Rathod vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190535101/
6 dislocation, 4) comminuted base of 3rd metacarpal fracture and 5) small displaced fracture near 2nd and 4th metacarpal base.
The same is deposed by P.W.2, who is the doctor who has clinically examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability.
On the other hand, there is no contrary or rebuttal evidence on record to disbelieve the above medical records of the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that,
the respondent No.1 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg.
No.TN-66-AE-1800 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
17. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) 11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

18. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

sentences.text: Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident occurred on 17-09-2023 at about 2:00 a.m., near 4th cross, 80 feet road, Sanjaynagara, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.TN-66-AE-1800.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Partly Affirmative.
20. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.TN-66-AE-1800 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

The medical records placed on record clearly speaks that, the petitioner has sustained 1) displaced intraarticular radius fracture left forearm, 2) displaced ulnar styloid fracture, 3) dislocated 2, 3, 4th carpametacarpal joints with dorsal metacarpal dislocation, 4)
comminuted base of 3rd metacarpal fracture and 5) small displaced fracture near 2nd and 4th metacarpal base and for the said injuries he has undergone surgeries.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants,
transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
21. Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.

To prove his Suyash Rathod vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190535101/
7 age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.11.

sentences.text: As per Ex.P.11, the date of birth of the petitioner is 10-11-2005.
The accident has taken place on 17-09-2023 at about 2:00 a.m.
This clearly goes to show that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 18 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered 1) displaced intraarticular radius fracture left forearm, 2) displaced ulnar styloid fracture, 3) dislocated 2, 3, 4th carpametacarpal joints with dorsal metacarpal dislocation, 4) comminuted base of 3rd metacarpal fracture and 5) small displaced fracture near 2nd and 4th metacarpal base.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that,
there is 34.62% physical disability of left upper limb and 11.54% physical disability to the whole body of the petitioner.

Further, the Ex.P.10 wound certificate and Ex.P.13 and 14 discharge summaries, Ex.P.15 outpatient case-sheet, Ex.P.17 OPD slip with clinical note and Ex.P.18 x-ray clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injuries and he has undergone surgeries for the said injuries.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, the petitioner has not suffered any disability and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 17-09-2023 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 23-12- 2025, which is after lapse of two years and three months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.

Further, it is pertinent to note that,
P.W.2 has clearly stated in his cross-examination that, the fracture of left ulnar styloid is non-union and all other fractures are united and dislocations are corrected, implants have been removed, left wrist movement are minimal decreased and there is only one grade loss of muscle power of left wrist joint and the petitioner can perform the day to day activities with some difficulties.

Therefore,
considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that,
considering the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
22. The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was student.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he has not been able to concentrate on his studies.
The respondent No.1 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove the same.
But, he has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was student.
Admittedly, the petitioner was having no income as on the date of accident.

In such circumstances, taking into consideration the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident, this Court is of the opinion that, the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is to be considered in the instant case.
The accident took place in 2023.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered at Rs.16,000/- per month, which comes to Rs.1,92,000/- per annum.

23. As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 18 years is 18.

24. Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.4,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 12 medical bills, as per Ex.P.16.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.1,10,650/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,10,650/- under the head of medical expenses.
25. Pain and sufferings:

In the present case, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e. 1)
displaced intraarticular radius fracture left forearm, 2) displaced ulnar styloid fracture, 3) dislocated 2, 3, 4th carpametacarpal joints with dorsal metacarpal dislocation, 4) comminuted base of 3rd metacarpal fracture and 5) small displaced fracture near 2nd and 4th metacarpal base.
As per Ex.P.3 and 14 discharge summaries, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 7 days from 18-09-2023 to 21-09-2023 and 19-06-2024 to 21-06-2024, in Suyog Hospital, Nagpur.
Further, as per P.W.2, the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.

In such circumstances,
certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.
Therefore, taking into consideration the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that,
an compensation amount of Rs.60,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
26. Attendant charges:
As per Ex.P.3 and 14 discharge summaries, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 7 days in Suyog Hospital, Nagpur.
He might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.

Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 7 =
Rs.7,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
27. Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.3 and 14 discharge summaries, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 7 days in Suyog Hospital, Nagpur.
He might have spent considerable amount towards food and nourishment during that period.

Therefore, compensation of Rs.800 x 7 =
Rs.5,600/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
28. Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Lottegollahalli, RMV Extension II Stage,
Bengaluru North, Bengaluru, the accident has occurred near 4th cross, 80 feet road, Sanjaynagara,
Bengaluru and he has taken treatment at Suyog Hospital, Nagpur.
Taking into consideration the distance in between the above places, compensation of Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
29. Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 7 days as in-patient at Suyog Hospital, Nagpur, for the grievous injuries sustained by him.
He might have taken rest for about 2 months and lost his income for the said period.

Therefore, Rs.16,000 x 2 =
Rs.32,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
30. Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 18 years and unfortunately he has suffered 1) displaced intraarticular radius fracture left forearm, 2) displaced ulnar styloid fracture, 3) dislocated 2, 3, 4th Suyash Rathod vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190535101/

Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
31. Future medical expenses:
There is no evidence on record to show that, the petitioner requires any further treatment for the injuries sustained in the said accident.
Even, the P.W.2 has not stated anything with respect to same.

Further, the P.W.2 in his cross-examination has clearly stated that,
the fractures are united and all the implants have been removed.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding future medical expenses does not arise at all.
Therefore, no compensation is awarded in this particular head.

32. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows:
1. Loss of future income Rs. 3,45,600-00 2.
Medical expenses 1,10,650-00 3. Pain and sufferings 60,000-00
4. Attendant charges 7,000-00 5. Food and nourishment 5,600-00 6.
Conveyance expenses 10,000-00 7. Loss of income during 32,000-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 40,000-00
9. Future medical expenses Nil
For the reasons stated supra, the petitioner is held liable for contributory negligence to the extent of 10%.

After deducting the said value from the total compensation amount, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,49,765/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization.
33. Liability: Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle bearing No.TN-66-AE-1800.

Further, as per the true copy of reply given by the owner of offending vehicle, to the notice issued by the investigation officer under Sec.133 of Motor Vehicles Act, which is marked as Ex.P.7, the driver of offending vehicle by name Gopikrishnan S/o P. As such, the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.1 in respect of offending vehicle was valid as on the date of accident i.e.
17-09-2023.
There is no evidence on record to show that, there is breach of any terms and conditions of the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.1.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg. No.TN-66-AE-1800 the accident in question has occurred and the petitioner has sustained simple injuries in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,49,765/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent No.1, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
34. Issue No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.5,49,765/- (Rupees five lakh forty nine thousand seven hundred and sixty five only), with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.1 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
There are every chances that, due to three persons traveling on a motorcycle, which is meant for two persons, there would be congestion to the rider of said motorcycle and he might have lost control resulting in the accident.
The petitioner being fully aware that, the said vehicle is meant for traveling of two persons,
he has taken risk of traveling triple on the said motorcycle.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that,
the petitioner is also liable for contributory negligence in the cause of accident.
But, as there is no evidence on record to show that, the very act of three persons riding on the motorcycle has directly contributed either to the accident or to the impact of the accident upon the victim, this Court is of the opinion that, holding the petitioner liable for contributory negligence to the extent of 10% would be justified and it will meet the ends of justice.
When the accident is not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KK-6021, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that,
the respondent No.1 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing Reg.
No.TN-66-AE-1800 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
17. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) 11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
18. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
